research_mode: official ONS, Home Office and Police.uk sources only; repeat-victimisation, sensitive self-completion, domestic-abuse measure transitions, outcome definitions and Police.uk identity or missing-location semantics; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Domestic-abuse series break
verified_claims: estimates from the new questions cannot be directly compared with estimates from previous questions
ONS does not provide an adjustment that makes the two series directly comparable
year ending March 2024 onwards uses the new measure
limitations: changes must not be described as real-world trends across the break
measure version is mandatory

sources.name: Outcome 15 definition
verified_claims: outcome 15 requires a named suspect
the victim supports police action
evidential difficulties prevent further action and can include a wanted suspect who cannot be traced
limitations: outcome 15 is not equivalent to no suspect
closure can remain pending further action

sources.name: Outcome 16 definition
verified_claims: outcome 16 requires a named suspect
the victim does not support or has withdrawn support from police action
it is a victim-based evidential-difficulties category
limitations: non-support must not be interpreted as absence of an offence
outcome 16 differs materially from outcome 15

sources.name: Outcome 18 definition
verified_claims: outcome 18 applies where no suspect is identified
the crime has been investigated as far as reasonably possible
the case is closed pending further investigative opportunities
limitations: closed does not mean permanently incapable of reopening
outcome 18 is not a safety score

sources.name: Outcomes for offences recorded in period
verified_claims: the cohort method follows offences recorded in a defined period
outcomes accumulate as investigations progress
the method is useful for offence types such as sexual offences that can take longer to close
limitations: recent cohorts are incomplete
rates change as the cohort matures

sources.name: Outcomes closed in reporting period
verified_claims: the closed-period method counts outcomes recorded in the reporting year
the associated crime may have been recorded in an earlier period
this measure differs from the recorded-offence cohort method
limitations: volumes mix crime cohorts
the two outcome views must not be merged without a bridge

sources.name: Outcome timeliness coverage exclusions
verified_claims: median days are calculated from record-level Home Office Data Hub data
force coverage can differ by table and offence group
forces with missing or quality-problem data are excluded from specified medians
limitations: median coverage is not uniform across every figure
excluded-force notes must accompany comparisons

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police.uk crime identifier contract
verified_claims: persistent_id is a 64-character crime identifier
the API id is not guaranteed to remain the same for a crime
the API id is not a police identifier
limitations: persistent_id stability does not validate spatial accuracy
identifier fields must not be interchanged

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police.uk crimes with no location contract
verified_claims: the endpoint returns crimes that could not be mapped to a location
location and location_type are null and location_subtype is empty
the latest available month is used when date is omitted
limitations: unmapped crimes are not zero crime
mutable latest-month defaults must be pinned

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police.uk unavailable-status category
verified_claims: status-update-unavailable is a documented outcome category
the category is distinct from under-investigation
absence of an update is represented explicitly
limitations: unavailable status is not evidence of no outcome
category and date must be retained separately
